new_entities.name: Dual orexin receptor antagonists for chronic insomnia
aliases: dual orexin antagonists for insomnia disorder
new_entities.description: Use of dual orexin receptor antagonists such as suvorexant, lemborexant, or daridorexant to improve sleep initiation in chronic insomnia.

new_entities.name: Sleep onset
new_entities.description: The timing and ease of falling asleep at the beginning of the night.

edges.effect_quant: A 2025 network meta-analysis of 8 placebo-controlled trials and 5,198 adults found all marketed DORAs improved subjective time to sleep onset, with the strongest primary-outcome estimate for lemborexant 10 mg (SMD -0.430, 95% CI -0.568 to -0.292) versus placebo. Earlier pooled phase-3 suvorexant data and long-term lemborexant phase-3 results support a durable class effect on sleep initiation.
edges.population: adults with chronic insomnia disorder, including both middle-aged and older adults in modern phase 3 registration trials
edges.mechanism: Dual orexin receptor antagonists reduce wake drive by blocking orexin signaling, allowing sleep to begin more readily without relying on broad GABAergic sedation.
edges.summary: This is a strong protective sleep-onset edge. Across modern randomized trials, DORAs consistently improve insomnia sleep-initiation endpoints, with some heterogeneity in magnitude by dose and individual agent.
edges.caveats: The class also affects sleep maintenance, so trial outcomes often blend initiation and maintenance benefits. Somnolence and next-day impairment remain relevant dose-dependent tradeoffs, and comparative advantage among individual DORAs is still being refined.

evidence.notes: Comparative efficacy and safety of daridorexant, lemborexant, and suvorexant for insomnia: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: Subjective time to sleep onset at month 1 for lemborexant 10 mg versus placebo in the network meta-analysis

evidence.citation: HerringWJ et al 2016 J Clin Sleep Med
